title: Add deprecation fields to model/version records + enforce validation constraints
author: Michael Nguyen
description:
Context: We need first-class deprecation metadata on model *versions* to support enterprise change-management and the upcoming customer-visible model changelog. Today we have ad-hoc notes in docs/Slack and no consistent way to represent sunset timelines or a suggested replacement.

This PR adds the v1 deprecation fields to the model registry schema and enforces constraints in server-side validation so we can safely migrate existing catalog entries and generate consistent downstream events.

What’s included: (1) Schema changes: Adds `deprecation` block to `ModelVersionRecord` (and plumbs through API structs) with: `sunset_date` (ISO-8601 date), `replacement_model` (model_id + optional version_id), and `customer_messaging` (customer-safe text). Field names match the draft schema naming used in the metadata schema v1 doc and are intentionally explicit to avoid ambiguity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. (2) Validation rules: Enforces that `sunset_date` must parse as YYYY-MM-DD and cannot be earlier than `deprecated_at` (when set); `replacement_model` cannot refer to the same {model_id, version_id} as the record being deprecated; if `sunset_date` is present, at least one of `replacement_model` or `customer_messaging` must be provided (so customers aren’t left without guidance); `customer_messaging` must be <= 800 chars, must not contain internal-only prefixes ("internal:", "ops:"), and must be plain text (no markdown links) to avoid leaking internal URLs at publish time (templating will own link rendering later). (3) API compatibility: Existing records remain valid; the new fields are optional and default to null/empty. Validation only triggers when the fields are present, or when a record is explicitly marked deprecated. (4) Tests: Adds unit tests for schema validation (date parsing, replacement self-reference, messaging limits) and golden fixtures for a deprecated version record.

Notes / follow-ups: This PR intentionally does not implement redaction/allowlisting for what can be emitted to the public changelog feed (tracked separately). It *does* ensure we have clean deprecation data in the registry and that invalid records can’t be written.

Operational impact: This is a schema-only change within the registry service. No migrations are required for existing rows; backfill tooling will populate these fields as part of the migration epic.

Risk: Low/medium. The main risk is rejecting updates that previously would have been accepted; mitigated by making fields optional and adding clear validation error messages. I also added a feature-flagged escape hatch in the admin CLI (`--allow-past-sunset-date`) for backfill of already-sunset legacy versions (used only by release engineering during migration).
commits: tests: add deprecation validation fixtures + table tests
admin: add allow-past-sunset-date override for backfill runs (guarded)
review_conversation: Quentin Harris: Can we clarify whether `sunset_date` is date-only or RFC3339 timestamp? We should avoid timezone ambiguity if customers interpret it differently.

Michael Nguyen (author): Good call. Updated to enforce date-only (YYYY-MM-DD) and added wording to docs/registry/schema_v1.md: “interpreted as end-of-day UTC for customer comms.” Validation now rejects timestamps.
Chloe Martin: Replacement model reference — do we allow specifying just model_id (no version_id) so PM can point to “latest”? If yes, how do we validate it exists?

Michael Nguyen (author): Yes: `replacement_model` supports model_id + optional version_id. Validation checks model_id is non-empty; if version_id provided, we validate it exists + is compatible. If version_id omitted, we accept and treat as “recommended model; resolver chooses default pinned stable version.” Added tests + error messages.
Jordan Lee: `customer_messaging` checks for internal prefixes seems brittle. Why not just make it internal-only until we add allowlisting/redaction?

Michael Nguyen (author): Agree it’s not perfect; added it as a lightweight guardrail because these fields are explicitly intended to be customer-visible later. I tightened it to a minimal set (rejects lines starting with "internal:" or "ops:") and added a TODO pointing to the public allowlist PR. If we prefer to drop this check entirely, I’m fine, but PM requested early protection due to SUP-18421 concerns.
Connor O'Brien: The `--allow-past-sunset-date` override makes sense for backfills, but I’d like it to be clearly scoped so it can’t be used by accident in normal updates.

Michael Nguyen (author): Updated: the override is only available in `registry-admin backfill` (not in normal update paths), and it logs an audit-style warning to stdout with the record IDs being written. Added a unit test to ensure normal API writes still reject past sunset dates unless deprecated_at is also past (legacy import path).
Chloe Martin: OpenAPI change adds new fields on the version record response. Is this a breaking change for older clients?
Michael Nguyen (author): Additive only; existing fields unchanged. Confirmed openapi-diff is “non-breaking.”
Quentin Harris: Looks good after the date-only change + tests. Approved.
Jordan Lee: Approved with note: we should revisit messaging validation once allowlisting lands.
release_notes: Internal: model registry schema now supports deprecation metadata (sunset_date, replacement_model, customer_messaging) with validation. Enables upcoming model changelog + enterprise change-management workflows.
